audits.title: Evaluation of emergency caesarean sections--completion of the audit cycle in a Central London teaching hospital.
audits.setting: Central London teaching hospital (Guy's and St Thomas')

cycle1.result: Total CS rate 20.9%; emergency CS 14.8%; failure to progress delivered within 1 hour 76%; fetal distress within 30 minutes 39%; cord pH documented 60%; ranitidine prescribed 53%; heparin 88%.

cycle2.result: Total CS rate 19.2%; emergency CS 13.6%; failure to progress within 1 hour 64%; fetal distress within 30 minutes 39%; cord pH documented 96%; ranitidine 81%; heparin 87%.

audits.other_findings: No effect on decision-to-delivery times or fetal blood sampling (41% vs 34% of fetal distress cases).
audits.citation: Bruce D, Stone S, Harding K. Evaluation of emergency caesarean sections--completion of the audit cycle in a Central London teaching hospital. J Obstet Gynaecol. 2002;22(3):273-278. doi:10.1080/01443610220130553. PMID: 12521498.

audits.title: Audit of 'crash' emergency caesarean sections due to cord prolapse in terms of response time and perinatal outcome.
audits.standard: Delivery within 30 minutes of diagnosis for crash caesarean section

cycle1.result: Median diagnosis to delivery 20 minutes (range 10 to 40); 76% (19/30) delivered within 30 minutes; time of diagnosis not recorded in 5 cases.

audits.citation: Tan WC, Tan LK, Tan HK, Tan AS. Audit of 'crash' emergency caesarean sections due to cord prolapse in terms of response time and perinatal outcome. Ann Acad Med Singap. 2003;32(5):638-641. doi:10.47102/annals-acadmedsg.v32n5p638. PMID: 14626792.

audits.title: Evaluation of surgical and anaesthesia response times for crash caesarean sections--an audit of a Singapore hospital.
audits.standard: RCOG Organisational Standards: decision-to-delivery within 30 minutes for urgent caesarean section

cycle1.result: Mean decision-to-delivery 7.7 min (SD 3.0); 100% within 17 minutes; mean decision-to-anaesthesia 3.5 min.

audits.other_findings: 88.8% had general anaesthesia; no difference in interval or cord pH by anaesthetic type; audit followed a 1997 crash CS protocol.
audits.citation: Lim Y, Shah MK, Tan HM. Evaluation of surgical and anaesthesia response times for crash caesarean sections--an audit of a Singapore hospital. Ann Acad Med Singap. 2005;34(10):606-610. doi:10.47102/annals-acadmedsg.v34n10p606. PMID: 16382245.

audits.title: Decision-to-Delivery Time Intervals in Emergency Caesarean Section Cases: Repeated cross-sectional study from Oman.
audits.standard: Decision-to-delivery interval ≤30 minutes for emergency caesarean section

cycle1.period: three months, between April 2011 and June 2013 (initial retrospective cycle)

audits.intervention: Improvement strategies addressing factors causing DDI delays.

cycle2.period: three months, between April 2011 and June 2013 (third cycle)
cycle2.result: DDI ≤30 minutes in 60.8% of 79 women (P value truncated in abstract).

audits.other_findings: Second cycle achieved 44.6% of 83 cases; DDI over 60 minutes was associated with more SCBU admissions and low Apgar scores.
audits.citation: Tashfeen K, Patel M, Hamdi IM, Al-Busaidi IHA, Al-Yarubi MN. Decision-to-Delivery Time Intervals in Emergency Caesarean Section Cases: Repeated cross-sectional study from Oman. Sultan Qaboos Univ Med J. 2017;17(1):e38-e42. doi:10.18295/squmj.2016.17.01.008. PMID: 28417027.

audits.title: An audit of the effect of case selection on compliance with a 30-minute audit standard for decision-to-delivery interval at category 1 caesarean section.
audits.standard: Local audit standard: 90% or more of category 1 caesarean sections with decision-to-delivery interval 30 minutes or less
audits.setting: St Michael's Hospital, Bristol; prospective audit

cycle1.result: Proportion with DDI >30 min ranged from 8.3% (30/362) to 21.9% (54/247) depending on case inclusion; 18.5% (42/227) when decided in labour room excluding failed operative vaginal delivery.

audits.other_findings: 158 had failed operative vaginal delivery in theatre and 43 had an urgency change; compliance depends heavily on inclusion criteria.
audits.citation: Kinsella SM. An audit of the effect of case selection on compliance with a 30-minute audit standard for decision-to-delivery interval at category 1 caesarean section. Int J Obstet Anesth. 2021;48:103214. doi:10.1016/j.ijoa.2021.103214. PMID: 34500189.

audits.title: Crash caesarean section audit: an important tool for an obstetric unit to ensure safe quality care.
audits.standard: Crash caesarean section delivery within 30 minutes of decision; indication appropriateness score
audits.setting: Tertiary maternity unit, KK Women's and Children's Hospital

cycle1.result: All 148 crash caesarean sections were within 30 minutes (mean 10.2 minutes); 21 (14.2%) scored above 1.5 for appropriateness of indication.

audits.other_findings: 15 maternal complications, 1 birth injury and 4 perinatal deaths; commonest indication non-reassuring fetal status (83/148).
audits.citation: Ng YHG, Tan LK, Wright A. Crash caesarean section audit: an important tool for an obstetric unit to ensure safe quality care. BMC Pregnancy Childbirth. 2025;25(1):1267. doi:10.1186/s12884-025-08203-w. PMID: 41291533.

audits.title: Crash Caesarean Delivery: How to Optimise Decision-to-Delivery Interval by Initiating a Novel Code? A Clinical Audit.
audits.standard: International standard 30 min decision-to-delivery interval; local CODE-10 target 15 min
audits.intervention: CODE-10 Crash Caesarean rapid response protocol (in place during the audit)
audits.other_findings: Transport delays caused both DDIs over 15 min; no difference between office and non-office hours.

audits.title: Improving decision-to-delivery interval for category 1 emergency caesarean births in a tertiary hospital.
audits.standard: Decision-to-delivery interval within 30 min for category 1 caesarean; institutional target over 90%
audits.setting: Tertiary hospital with shared theatres, Singapore General Hospital

cycle1.result: Local audit showed inconsistent compliance with the 30-min standard.

audits.intervention: Reinforced categorisation, anaesthetist awareness of interval expectations and standardised workflow posters for activation and escalation.
audits.other_findings: No maternal or neonatal adverse events or theatre disruption.
audits.citation: Ang VWL, Chee DY, Yap SH, Liew WJ, Lau WK. Improving decision-to-delivery interval for category 1 emergency caesarean births in a tertiary hospital. Anaesth Rep. 2026;14(1):e70051. doi:10.1002/anr3.70051. PMID: 41695079.
